variants.maintainer_notes: Device selection (2026-11-04): --busdev-num ${BUS}:${DEV} added so openFPGALoader opens the device the engine chose, not the first one with these USB IDs. Low risk, so tested is unchanged: openFPGALoader's FTDI drivers (MPSSE, bitbang, CH552) open the device by bus and address when given (src/ftdipp_mpsse.cpp, ftdi_usb_open_bus_addr); not tried on hardware. USB filter (2026-11-05): release 0500. The board's USB debugger is a BL702 (Sipeed wiki, Update debugger page: BL702 on Tang Nano 1K, 4K, 9K and Primer 20K; BL616 on Nano 20K), which acts like an FT2232C/D and reports bcdDevice 0500: sipeed/RV-Debugger-BL702 firmware/app/usb2uartjtag/usb_descriptor.c (1b27d3f, FTDI_BCD_DEVICE 0x0500, "known full-speed FT2232C/D"), and a real Tang Nano 9K (openFPGALoader issue #382, rev 5.00). The BL702 is a full-speed device, and libftdi picks its packet size from bcdDevice, so its firmware can't claim to be an FT2232H (0700). Rules out the many boards with a real FT2232H. USB filter (2026-11-05): product name JTAG Debugger. Sipeed's BL702 debugger firmware reports manufacturer SIPEED and product JTAG Debugger (sipeed/RV-Debugger-BL702 firmware/app/usb2uartjtag/usb_descriptor.c, string descriptors 1 and 2; its emulated FTDI EEPROM says Open-EC, USB Debugger, which USB doesn't report), and Sipeed's Update debugger page offers one BL702 firmware for Tang Nano 1K, 4K, 9K and Primer 20K. Seen on a real Primer 20K (openFPGALoader issues #300, #573) and 9K (#382). Generic (Sipeed's stand-alone debuggers report it too), so the match is possible, not strong.
variants.user_notes: Other Sipeed boards with the same USB debugger chip report the same name, JTAG Debugger.
